subject: english
question:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

If you have / faith in God, / everything turn out / to be all right.
solution:
The correct answer is '**everything turn out**'.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The segment "**everything turn out**" lacks the correct verb form to agree with the subject "**everything**".
 
• The subject "**everything**" is singular, so the verb must be in the third person singular present tense form to match. The correct phrase should be "**everything turns out**."
 
• The verb "**turn**" needs an '**s**' at the end to correctly conjugate with the singular subject in present tense.

Therefore, the correct answer is ‘**Option 2**'.

 

**Correct Sentence**: *If you have faith in God, **everything turns out** to be all right.*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• "**If you have**" correctly sets up a conditional clause, indicating that the following statement is contingent upon the condition of having faith in God.
 
• "**faith in God**," is correctly phrased, with the preposition "in" showing the object of the faith.
 
• "**to be all right**" correctly concludes the sentence, indicating the outcome or result of having faith in God. The phrase is grammatically correct and completes the meaning of the sentence with a positive conclusion.
